core.title: Plan each component with at most 5 methods; split it when more are needed
core.given: A plan artifact you are authoring, revising or reviewing declares a component and its methods (new or existing)
core.when: You plan or review any component, whatever the edit — adding, removing or leaving its methods unchanged
core.then: Keep every component at 5 methods or fewer; if the capability needs more methods, split it into several focused components instead of exceeding the cap.
prefer: Split an over-full component along business-capability lines so each resulting component owns one capability with ≤ 5 methods
Keep a component small and focused, e.g. a validator with 3 methods (validate, eligibility check, explain)
avoid: A single component with 9 (or any > 5) methods — split it into focused components
Leaving an existing over-limit component as-is, or trimming it to a count still above 5 (e.g. 9 → 6), and treating that as compliant
Gaming the cap by merging distinct operations into one catch-all method or moving methods into an unnamed helper bag instead of splitting by capability
core.why: Capping a component at 5 methods keeps it focused on a single business capability; exceeding it signals the component is doing too much and should be split.
evidence: Count the methods declared for each component in the plan artifacts (new and existing); every count is ≤ 5
Where a capability needed more than 5 methods, the plan artifact shows it split into multiple focused components
verification: Check: count the methods declared for each component in the plan artifacts; a component with 6 or more declared methods is a finding. The condition is method count ≤ 5, and it applies to every declared component — not only those whose method list changed in the edit (an over-limit component that is merely trimmed, e.g. 9 → 6, remains a finding).
A finding carries the fix hint: split the component if more methods are needed.
No automated implementation exists in the source (implementation type none); detection requires a new observer that counts declared methods per component.
Activation requires a planning-phase observer (needs_new_observer) to know that a planner is authoring, revising or reviewing a plan artifact.

fires: Planner declares a new component with 6 or more methods
Planner adds a method to an existing component that already has 5 methods
Planner revises or reviews an artifact containing an existing component with more than 5 methods, even if its method list is unchanged (e.g. only its description is edited)
Planner reduces a component from 9 methods to 6 — still over the cap
doesNotFire: A planned component declares 5 or fewer methods
Planner edits the description of a component that already has 5 or fewer methods
Artifacts that do not declare components (e.g. acceptance wording only)

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral already: it constrains plan artifacts, not code. The numeric cap (5) is a parameter of the convention itself, not stack structure, so it stays in the core rather than becoming a profile key. The Bun-specific content is limited to realization details: the term ids/labels (max_methods, action), the project-specific example (OptionValidator), and the concrete plan-artifact kind names (component spec, plan, wagon), the last of which is supplied through the existing profile key roles.plan_artifact.kinds. bun.json's prefer[1] had already neutralized the project example, so the core keeps that neutral wording; the verbatim project example remains only in the Bun realization.
